chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: The Smith sisters and Mattie Hite at the Nest Club
summary: Mamie, Clara and Trixie Smith sang at the Nest Club, but Mattie Hite, who sang Stop It Joe, was considered the greatest cabaret entertainer.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: And they had about five or six entertainers all the time. One time when I was there with Harry White, they had Mamie Smith, Clara Smith... They weren't sisters, because they mentioned it, both of them. "She ain't no sister of mine," Clara said, and Mamie said, "God, she ain't no sister of mine." That's all the Smith sisters. There was Mamie Smith, Clara Smith, and later, in about two or three weeks, Trixie Smith, who worked with Miss Bargorne for Mae West. All those were Blues singers. There was Margie Sith(?). Mattie Hite later, who was... Mattie Hite was considered the greatest entertainer, Black entertainer, cabaret entertainer of all of them.

Mattie Hite. Everybody went to see Mattie Hite. She sang a song, "Stop It Joe." It was a fast thing. [SNAPS FINGERS] "Stop it, Joe." [SINGS, SNAPS] "Stop it, Joe." It was a fast thing she did. And she went from table to table, see. And she'd pick up the money, you know. They'd put it on the edge of the table with the bottle, you know, the Coca-Cola bottle. But she wouldn't do that. She said, "Give me that money. I ain't puttin' an act for nobody." And she was a dynamic woman, and highly respected. They'd say, "Mattie Hite's coming to work, Mattie Hite's coming to work." All them other big-time entertainers for
some reason acknowledged that Mattie Hite was the greatest. Now, you should check on some more performers later about Mattie Hite.
